heroHeadline: Iran Unveils Formal Hormuz Toll Plan; Trump Warns 'Very Bad Time'; Drone Strikes UAE Barakah Nuclear Plant; Pakistan Mediates; IDF Strikes Lebanon — Day 79
heroSubtitle: Day 79 (May 17): Iran formally unveiled a structured Hormuz toll and traffic management plan, with legislator Azizi describing a 'professional mechanism' with fees for Strait transit — only vessels cooperating with Iran will be permitted — and First VP Aref declaring Iran will block 'enemy' military equipment. European nations reportedly began direct negotiations with the IRGC Navy about transit terms. President Trump issued a sharp warning that Iran would have a 'very bad time' if a peace deal is not reached soon, with aides signaling resumed major combat operations are 'more seriously' under consideration. Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran to facilitate stalled US-Iran peace talks. A drone struck a generator at the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant — the Arab world's first operational nuclear power station — with UAE authorities confirming radiation levels remained normal and operations were unaffected. Israel struck Zawtar al-Sharqiyah in southern Lebanon; one IDF officer was killed, the 21st Israeli fatality since the Lebanon front opened March 2. The USS Gerald R. Ford returned to Virginia after an 11-month deployment — the carrier that opened Operation Epic Fury on February 28 has completed its war rotation.
